title: Google Cloud Digital Leader

intro.about: The Google Cloud Digital Leader certification validates that you can articulate the capabilities of Google Cloud's core products and services and explain how they benefit an organization — the judgment of a leader who shapes cloud decisions, not the hands of an engineer who implements them. The exam guide in force (launched August 12, 2026) defines six weighted sections: Digital Transformation with Google Cloud (~18%), Exploring Data Transformation (~18%), Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence (~18%), Modernize Infrastructure and Applications (~18%), Trust and Security (~18%), and Scaling with Google Cloud Operations (~10%).
intro.audience: Aimed at people who collaborate on, sponsor or steer cloud adoption rather than build it — business leaders, program and project managers, product owners, sales and partner roles, analysts, and anyone whose job is to connect a business problem to what Google Cloud can do about it. Google states no prerequisites and no hands-on requirement: every objective asks you to explain, describe, identify or differentiate, never to configure or deploy.

intro.disclaimer: An independent, originally-authored study tool for personal exam preparation — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Google LLC or its testing partners. "Google Cloud", "Google" and "Cloud Digital Leader" are trademarks of Google LLC. Every question was written clean-room from documented derivation artefacts against the public exam guide, with prior practice sets analyzed for classification only — and no answer key was taken from any source — exactly as this package's README records. Nothing here is drawn from the live Cloud Digital Leader item bank: real exam content is confidential under the Google Cloud certification exam terms, which bind you too once you sit the exam — please never share live questions here.

format_coverage: The real Cloud Digital Leader exam uses two item formats: multiple choice and multiple select. Mockka supports three, so this exam's format profile is a SUBSET of what the player can render rather than an excess — nothing about the real paper goes unrepresented. Multiple choice maps exactly to single_choice; multiple select maps to multiple_response, and Mockka scores it all-or-nothing. Mockka's third format, scenario_matching, has NO counterpart on the real exam and is set to zero throughout: you will not be asked to map scenarios onto a reused option set when you sit the real paper. Two limits you should know about. First, Google publishes no per-format count, and its own free sample-question set is 100% single choice — so the real share of multiple-select items is unpublished and unobserved, and the roughly 10% split used here (one choose-2-of-5 item per section) is Mockka's judgment, not a vendor figure. Second, the real exam is delivered as 50-60 questions in 90 minutes and Google does not publish a passing score (results are pass/fail only); this mock is built to the published upper bound of 60 items and applies a Mockka-chosen 70% pass threshold, which is a study aid and not a prediction of the real result.
